estimates.outcome: AUT average semantic distance among a participant’s own responses
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: spaCy en_core_web_md response embeddings; mean of all pairwise cosine distances (one minus cosine similarity) within each participant's set of responses. This measures variety within a person's own ideas, coded flexibility rather than across-person diversity. PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1771), Section III.C Measures. Aggregation across task rounds is not specified.

stats.difference_is: NoAI minus Low randomness (control minus treatment); regression coefficient preserved as printed

regression.model: Regression on HighRandomness and NoAI indicators, controlling for duration_seconds and AI_used; Low randomness is the omitted reference condition. Estimator and standard-error method are not stated. The printed coefficient is AUT_NoAI minus AUT_Low (control minus treatment).

sources.locator: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 1773), Table II, NoAI row, Avg Semantic Distance column; table note identifies standard errors in parentheses

estimates.notes: The NoAI coefficient is opposite to the named AI-versus-no-AI contrast; its printed negative sign is retained under the transcription rule. Downstream code must account for the control-minus-treatment orientation. Condition coefficients adjust for actual AI use, a post-assignment variable, so they are not unadjusted assignment effects. The regression sample size and whether observations are participants or participant-rounds are not printed. Table I cell counts are retained in the study record, not assumed to be the counts for this regression. Standard errors are printed, but their independent-unit basis cannot be established; se_basis=not_reported denotes this missing basis, not an absent numerical SE. No exact p-value is given for these unstarred coefficients; no bound is inferred.

estimates.outcome: DAT mean semantic distance among the words a participant generated
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Mean pairwise cosine distance between the words each participant generated, using the same spaCy en_core_web_md procedure as the AUT. This measures semantic breadth within a participant, coded flexibility rather than across-person diversity. PDF p. 3 (printed p. 1772), Section III.C Measures, continuing PDF p. 2. sources.quote: for the DAT, no coefficients were significant, so we do not report them

estimates.notes: Eligible full-sample contrast retained with null statistics: the authors explicitly omit DAT coefficients because none was significant. The individual contrasts follow the condition-indicator specification shown for the other tasks and the reconciled screening form; the DAT coefficients themselves are not printed. No means, SDs, SEs, exact p-values, or analysis counts are supplied, and no p-value bound is inferred from nonsignificance. The described model adjusts for time on task and actual AI use. The observation unit, aggregation across rounds, and uncertainty basis are not specified.

estimates.outcome: RAT accuracy (proportion of attempted problems answered correctly)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Number of correct responses divided by the total number of problems attempted (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1771, Section III.C Measures). The paper does not explain how responses were judged correct. automated_score is the screening form’s explicitly flagged placeholder: the codebook offers no matching measure code for accuracy on a test with correct answers. Convergent outcome; not eligible for pooling with creativity scores. Regression outcome is the raw accuracy proportion.

sources.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 1772), Section V Discussion, paragraph beginning "We did observe a few interesting results"
sources.quote: LLMs (irrespective of their level of randomness in the 0.1- 1.2 range) increase accuracy (on average, from 45 to 55%, p < .05).

estimates.notes: This is the Discussion’s full-sample comparison of AI availability, pooling both randomness conditions, before its separate AI-user subsample results. Means are percentages as printed; no difference is calculated. The paragraph supplies no comparison-specific people counts, analysis unit, SD, SE, confidence interval, or test statistic. Study-level arm counts are recorded separately. The nearby AI-availability denominator in the usage analysis is not treated as a printed N for this accuracy comparison. The p-value is a bound only. Section IV states that "this and all following results" use Holm-adjusted p-values, which appears to include this Discussion result, although the test and adjustment family are not described.

open_items: The number actually randomized and per-arm counts at assignment are not printed. Recruitment and analyzed counts cannot establish when exclusions occurred.

Tables II and III do not print regression N, estimator, observation unit, standard-error method, or clustering. The paper defines participant response-set scores but does not establish whether analysis rows are participants or participant-rounds. unit is null and the unknown SE basis is flagged as not_reported; numerical regression SEs are still retained.

The NoAI coefficients in Tables II and III are control minus treatment for the named Low-AI-versus-no-AI contrasts. Their signs are preserved as printed; any downstream treatment-minus-control effect must explicitly account for this orientation.
The condition regressions adjust for actual AI use, which is post-assignment. No equivalent unadjusted AUT or task-specific RAT condition contrasts are printed.
AUT and DAT participant-level SDs and full-sample arm means are not printed. No performance SDs are reported for RAT. No standardized effect can be transcribed.
DAT regression coefficients and uncertainty are deliberately omitted as nonsignificant; the four eligible DAT outcome-contrast records therefore contain null statistics.
The paper does not say whether semantic-distance scores pool responses across rounds or are calculated separately for each round.
The pooled AI-versus-no-AI RAT accuracy comparison supplies percentage means and a p-value bound, but no comparison-specific counts, SD, SE, test statistic, confidence interval, or analysis unit.

The measure vocabulary has no explicit code for correct-answer test accuracy; automated_score is retained only as the screening form’s labeled placeholder for RAT. Review 1 permits convergent outcomes on study pages, never in pooled creativity estimates.
Whether the regression-table significance stars follow the Results section’s Holm-adjustment statement is not clear; no p-value is inferred from absent stars.
The LLM model, provider, release year, participant country, and any preregistration are not identified.
The retrieval and citation records identify the open MIPRO proceedings copy as current, but its identity with the IEEE-formatted version of record has not been checked page by page.
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-10. Extractor A read the entire markdown conversion and extracted text from every page of the PDF, including the references; no appendix or supplement is present or referenced. Tables II and III were additionally checked with pymupdf.find_tables(). All quantitative estimate fields are transcribed without sign reversal, unit conversion, summed counts, or derived differences. One experiment is retained, matching the screening study identifier; task-specific contrasts compare assigned AI conditions within each task. The study recruited 960 people and analyzed 775 after exclusions (PDF p. 3, printed p. 1772, Section III.D); the recruitment count is not treated as the randomization count. The pilot was separate. Arm counts come from Table I. Estimate-specific Ns remain null where the exact statistic’s analysis sample is not printed. AI use was optional. AUT and DAT distances measure variation within a person’s responses, so they answer with_ai and are coded flexibility, not across_people. No after_ai or across_people outcome is reported. The paper calls mean and maximum distance primary metrics but reports no preregistration, so preregistered_primary is not_stated. No sample overlap with another paper is reported. No full-sample High-versus-NoAI contrast or combined-AI AUT/DAT statistic is constructed from other coefficients.
